newsitem.title: FRANCE: Synthelbao in cancer drug deal with U.S. firm.
newsitem.headline: Synthelbao in cancer drug deal with U.S. firm.

text.p: French pharmaceuticals company Synthelabo on Monday announced an exclusive licensing agreement for the development and marketing of cancer-related drug PPI-149 with U.S. biotechnology company Praecis Pharmaceuticals Inc.
Synthelabo said in a statement it was paying up to $68 million in the main part of the deal, and had also taken a $10 million equity stake in Praecis.
Under the deal the two firms will jointly continue the development of PPI-149, which is currently undergoing phase I and II clinical trials for prostate cancer, Synthelabo said.
Synthelabo will market the drug in Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and some African countries.
"In consideration of this licensing agreement, Synthelabo has made an upfront payment and will make further payments on achievement of specific development milestones," Synthelabo said.
"Such payments could reach up to $68 million. In addition, Praecis Pharmaceuticals Inc will receive a contribution to development costs and royalties on sales," it said.
"Moreover, Synthelabo has made a $10 million equity investment in Praecis Pharmaeuticals Inc."
